title: Lefkara Lace
summary: Lefkaritika is the white needlework of the village of Pano Lefkara in the Cypriot hills. Makers pull threads out of a square of linen, wrap and stitch the bars that remain into small diamonds, crosses and stars, and finish the edge with a narrow hem of tiny stitches. The geometry is counted, so the cloth repeats evenly in quarter turns.
howToPlay: Pick a thread colour and a stitch from the tray under the linen.
Touch a square to work that stitch: it is repeated on the squares where a quarter turn of the cloth would show it again.
Copy the small cloth shown above, then press Check.
rules: The cloth repeats in quarter turns, so each stitch you place is also worked on up to three partner squares.
A square counts only when its stitch and its thread colour both match the cloth you are copying.
Three stars need a nearly perfect copy; you can undo or clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: Lefkaritika has been made for centuries by the women of Pano Lefkara and nearby villages, and is recognised internationally as living cultural heritage. Its craft names include the drawn-thread work called dafna and the cut-linen style called tayiadha.
